meta.title: Hearing Intelligence Atlas
meta.subtitle: Realtime audio, hearing augmentation and assistive listening
meta.methodology: Ecosystem value is an editorial 0–100 score combining technical relevance, deployability, evidence, openness and influence. It is not a market valuation. Validation distinguishes independent human or clinical evidence from benchmark-only and manufacturer-reported results. GitHub stars and Hugging Face downloads are refreshed from their public APIs when the site is built.

fields.label: Speech enhancement
fields.description: Noise and reverberation reduction for clearer speech.

fields.label: Target speaker
fields.description: Select, enroll or track the voice the listener wants.

fields.label: Spatial & binaural
fields.description: Beamforming, binaural cues and spatial awareness.

fields.label: Evidence & datasets
fields.description: Challenges, clinical tests, human studies and corpora.

fields.label: Edge deployment
fields.description: Streaming runtimes, efficient networks and device constraints.

nodes.label: Melina
nodes.description: Local-first realtime hearing enhancement for Android and desktop. One audio core, nine switchable backends and measurable session telemetry.

validation.summary: Real-device Pixel and desktop benchmarks; clinical benefit is not yet established.

nodes.label: Google Research
nodes.description: A leading source of ultra-low-latency hearing architectures: Deep FIR, Googlears, differentiable auditory-loss compensation and source separation.

validation.summary: Strong research evidence; availability varies by project.

nodes.label: Australian Future Hearing Initiative
nodes.description: Google, Macquarie University and National Acoustic Laboratories collaboration on personalized hearing and differentiable auditory-loss compensation.

validation.summary: DAL is promising, but hardware and clinical validation remain future work.

nodes.label: UW Mobile Intelligence Lab
nodes.description: Shyam Gollakota's lab builds deployable semantic, binaural and enrolled-speaker listening systems, including ClearBuds and Look Once to Hear.

validation.summary: Multiple in-the-wild prototypes and controlled human studies.

nodes.label: Hearvana AI
nodes.description: Acoustic-intelligence startup co-founded by Shyam Gollakota to transfer UW work on programmable hearing, target speech and embedded audio AI into products.

validation.summary: The founding research portfolio is unusually strong; company product architecture and independent commercial validation are not public.

nodes.label: Clarity Project
nodes.description: The most directly relevant open evaluation ecosystem for hearing-aid speech enhancement, listener simulation and intelligibility prediction.

validation.summary: Listener-aware challenge design and public evaluation tooling.

nodes.label: Oldenburg · HörTech
nodes.description: Long-running open hearing-aid research hub behind openMHA, reference algorithms and low-latency binaural processing.

validation.summary: Hearing-science platform used in academic and translational studies.

nodes.label: Microsoft Research
nodes.description: Systematic work showing that carefully trained 3 ms CRUSE-class enhancement can approach 20 ms systems.

validation.summary: Strong controlled study; the ultra-low-latency weights are not public.

nodes.label: Columbia NAPLab
nodes.description: Nima Mesgarani's lab develops neuro-steered speaker extraction and real-time brain-controlled hearing.

validation.summary: Real-time study with invasive iEEG; compelling evidence but not a consumer sensing path.

nodes.label: Xiph.Org · Valin
nodes.description: Origin of RNNoise and PercepNet: compact recurrent enhancement designs with an exceptional deployment-to-compute ratio.

validation.summary: Widely deployed open implementations and peer-reviewed perceptual research.

nodes.label: CEVA
nodes.description: Edge-AI semiconductor IP company that open-sourced the DPDFNet family for highly efficient denoising.

validation.summary: Open weights and implementation; hearing-specific benefit is unvalidated.

nodes.label: Alibaba IIC Speech Lab
nodes.description: Maintains ClearerVoice Studio, pretrained enhancement, separation, super-resolution and target-speaker extraction models.

validation.summary: Broad public model coverage and reproducible objective metrics; not optimized for hearing-aid latency.

nodes.label: Sonova · Phonak
nodes.description: Global hearing-care group. Phonak commercialized dedicated deep speech processing and acquired Audatic's research team.

validation.summary: Large commercial deployment; technical details and model weights remain proprietary.

nodes.label: WS Audiology · Signia · Widex
nodes.description: Global hearing-aid group combining Signia's conversation-centric processing with Widex sound-quality systems.

validation.summary: Product-scale validation; core AI architecture is proprietary.

nodes.label: Demant · Oticon
nodes.description: Hearing-care group behind Oticon's DNN-based open-sound processing and extensive audiology research.

validation.summary: Substantial hearing research and commercial evidence; models are closed.

nodes.label: GN Hearing · ReSound
nodes.valueLabel: €2.3B enterprise value in the announced 2026 Amplifon transaction
nodes.description: Hearing-aid platform known for connectivity, binaural directionality and recent dedicated AI processing.

validation.summary: Commercial-scale evidence; exact network details are proprietary.

nodes.label: Starkey
nodes.description: Independent hearing-aid manufacturer integrating neural processing, sensors and health features on-device.

validation.summary: Commercial deployment with proprietary models.

nodes.label: Apple
nodes.description: Made hearing assistance a mass-market OS and earbud capability through AirPods Pro and clinically validated hearing features.

validation.summary: Regulated over-the-counter hearing-aid feature; internal processing remains closed.

nodes.label: Audatic
nodes.description: Berlin deep-learning hearing startup whose research and team became part of Sonova/Phonak.

validation.summary: Published research influenced a commercial product; weights and training data are unavailable.

nodes.label: Fortell
nodes.description: Spatial-AI hearing startup focused on separating and rendering conversational sound scenes.

validation.summary: Interesting positioning; limited public technical and independent validation detail.

nodes.label: Orka Labs
nodes.description: Consumer hearing company publishing a low-latency multi-stage enhancement architecture derived from Clarity work.

validation.summary: Strong challenge result, with a documented generalization gap on the evaluation set.

nodes.label: Bose Research
nodes.description: Published TinyLSTM and personalized PercepNet work targeting low-compute hearables and hearing enhancement.

validation.summary: Relevant perceptual studies; implementations and weights are not consistently public.

nodes.label: GTCRN Fast
nodes.description: Ultra-light streaming speech enhancement with grouped temporal convolutions and recurrent paths. The fast 16 kHz ONNX variant is bundled in Melina.

validation.summary: Strong efficiency and objective benchmark results; not hearing-loss-specific.

nodes.label: RNNoise 0.2
nodes.description: Classic hybrid DSP/RNN suppressor. Tiny, stable and 48 kHz native; a vital baseline when latency and battery matter more than SOTA scores.

validation.summary: Mature production use and perceptual evaluation.

nodes.label: UL-UNAS Stream
nodes.description: Architecture-searched ultra-light streaming denoiser, included in Melina through sherpa-onnx.

validation.summary: Efficient open model; limited hearing-specific evaluation.

nodes.label: DeepFilterNet3
nodes.description: Full-band 48 kHz neural filtering with perceptually motivated ERB features. Melina includes a high-quality desktop backend.

validation.summary: Strong open full-band baseline with deployable Rust/C API.

nodes.label: DPDFNet 2 · 4 · 8
nodes.description: A scalable CEVA denoising family. Melina exposes three 16 kHz sizes plus a 48 kHz HQ variant to explore the quality/compute curve.

validation.summary: Open, compact and measurable on-device; hearing benefit remains to validate.

nodes.label: Classic DSP
nodes.description: Deterministic low-cost baseline in Melina: filtering, dynamics and gain staging without neural inference.

validation.summary: Transparent and stable; less selective than neural enhancement.

nodes.label: Silero VAD
nodes.description: Compact voice activity detector used as a control signal in Melina, not as an enhancer.

validation.summary: Mature open VAD with broad language and noise coverage.

nodes.label: TEN VAD
nodes.description: Efficient VAD available as an optional Melina backend. Its additional license restrictions require careful distribution review.

validation.summary: Promising realtime VAD; license is less permissive than MIT/BSD alternatives.

nodes.label: Semantic Hearing
nodes.description: Binaural causal system that lets a listener choose among 20 semantic sound classes while preserving spatial cues.

validation.summary: Public code/checkpoint and real connected-smartphone latency.

nodes.label: Look Once to Hear
nodes.description: Enrolls a target voice from a brief visual/audio cue, then tracks and extracts it in realtime on a mobile device.

validation.summary: Code and training pipeline are public; license is non-commercial.

nodes.label: Aurchestra
nodes.description: Fine-grained soundscape control for augmented hearing: separates up to five active sound classes into independently mixable realtime streams on constrained edge platforms.

validation.summary: MobiSys 2026 Best Artifact; open code, checkpoints and a public 125 GB binaural dataset setup.

nodes.label: Proactive Hearing Assistant
nodes.description: Automatically infers the wearer's conversation partners from self-speech, turn-taking and dialogue dynamics, without manual enrollment or prompts.

validation.summary: Evaluated on 6.8 hours of real two- and three-speaker egocentric conversations; open code, model card and training dataset.

nodes.label: TF-MLPNet
nodes.description: Tiny mixed-precision realtime speech separation network built for low-power neural accelerators in hearables and hearing aids.

metrics.latencyMs: <6 ms inference on GAP9; 6 ms chunks

validation.summary: Demonstrated in realtime on GAP9 with a 3.5–4× runtime reduction over prior streaming separators; turnkey model packaging is limited.

nodes.label: Sound Bubble
nodes.description: Creates a programmable 1–2 metre listening bubble: speech inside remains audible while voices and noise outside are suppressed.

metrics.latencyMs: 12 ms algorithmic; 6.36 ms compute for 8 ms chunk

validation.summary: Open training code/checkpoint path and real-world evaluation in unseen environments and wearers; reports 49 dB outside-bubble suppression.

nodes.label: Waveformer
nodes.description: Low-latency target-sound extraction architecture that became a reference baseline for semantic and fine-grained augmented hearing.

validation.summary: Public code and model; now outperformed by Aurchestra variants but valuable as a causal baseline.

nodes.label: HybridBeam
nodes.description: Hybrid neural beamforming for on-device directional hearing, combining learned acoustic inference with controllable spatial processing.

validation.summary: Public AAAI implementation and an important precursor to later UW programmable-hearing systems.

nodes.label: Deep FIR
nodes.description: Google hearing-aid architecture that directly predicts minimum-phase FIR filters for sub-millisecond algorithmic latency.

validation.summary: Excellent latency/quality point; no public training code or weights.

nodes.label: Googlears
nodes.description: Low-latency neural multiframe beamforming plus adaptive equalization designed for hearing aids.

validation.summary: Relevant end-to-end hearing architecture; no public weights.

nodes.label: Differentiable Auditory Loss Compensation
nodes.description: Trains enhancement through differentiable normal/impaired cochlear models, optimizing toward what a listener with hearing loss can recover.

validation.summary: Compelling objective; hardware and clinical testing are explicitly future work.

nodes.label: 3 ms CRUSE
nodes.description: Microsoft study configuration demonstrating that latency-aware training can make a 3 ms model competitive with 20 ms enhancement.

validation.summary: Well-controlled latency study; weights and implementation are not released.

nodes.label: RT-Tango
nodes.description: Realtime binaural enhancement combining efficient neural masks with a spatial distortion-weighted multichannel Wiener filter.

validation.summary: Excellent architecture target; no official code or weights found.

nodes.label: MN-TANGO
nodes.description: Extreme-efficiency TANGO derivative targeting tiny always-on audio hardware.

validation.summary: Exceptional efficiency claims; implementation and weights are unavailable.

nodes.label: NeuralAids
nodes.description: Energy-aware neural hearing-aid prototype reporting realtime MCU-class performance.

validation.summary: Promising power and latency; no public model code.

nodes.label: CoFi-Lite
nodes.description: Ultra-lightweight speech enhancement accepted to IEEE SPL. Repository exists, but code and weights await commercial IP review.

validation.summary: Official repository targets a January 2027 academic release.

nodes.label: DTLN
nodes.description: Two-stage time-frequency/time-domain recurrent denoiser and an important open low-latency baseline.

validation.summary: Mature reproducible baseline; latency is above strict hearing-aid targets.

nodes.label: ClearerVoice Studio
nodes.description: Large open suite spanning FRCRN, MossFormer2 enhancement/separation, super-resolution and audiovisual target extraction.

validation.summary: Excellent research and adaptation source; most models are not strict realtime hearing architectures.

nodes.label: TIGER
nodes.description: Efficient time-frequency interleaved speaker separation architecture relevant to target-speaker research, but not designed around hearing-aid latency.

validation.summary: Strong separation results; deployment path requires causal redesign.

nodes.label: ClearBuds
nodes.description: Synchronized wireless binaural microphones plus lightweight mobile neural separation, evaluated in the wild.

validation.summary: 1,041 ratings and 15.4 hours of in-the-wild evaluation.

nodes.label: PercepNet
nodes.description: Perceptually motivated full-band enhancement using ERB-band gains and pitch filtering, designed for low complexity.

validation.summary: Strong perceptual basis and low delay; canonical public packaging is less direct than RNNoise.

nodes.label: Personalized PercepNet
nodes.description: Conditions PercepNet on a target-speaker representation to suppress competing talkers while retaining low complexity.

validation.summary: Highly relevant personalization concept; no turnkey public weights.

nodes.label: Bose TinyLSTMs
nodes.description: Structured compression and pruning for tiny recurrent speech enhancement on constrained hearables.

validation.summary: Useful efficient design evidence; no maintained turnkey model.

nodes.label: Orka multi-stage enhancer
nodes.description: Clarity-derived multi-stage system combining denoising, dereverberation and hearing-loss compensation.

validation.summary: Top-five development result with poor evaluation-set generalization documented by the authors.

nodes.label: Brain-controlled hearing
nodes.description: Real-time auditory attention decoding steers speech separation toward the attended speaker using intracranial neural signals.

validation.summary: Improved intelligibility and listening effort; invasive sensing prevents direct consumer deployment.

nodes.label: Conv-TasNet WHAMR
nodes.description: Public SpeechBrain-derived WHAMR checkpoint with unusual human hearing results. Binary inspection shows non-causal global normalization: it is not a 1 ms realtime model.

validation.summary: Reported +0.8 dB benefit for hearing-impaired and +5.7 dB for cochlear-implant listeners, but −0.9 dB for normal hearing; deployability is a red flag.

nodes.label: Phonak DEEPSONIC
nodes.description: Dedicated DNN chip and speech-from-noise pipeline in Phonak Sphere products; trained on a manufacturer-reported 22 million sound samples.

validation.summary: Manufacturer reports up to 10 dB SNR improvement; architecture and weights are closed.

nodes.label: Signia Integrated Xperience
nodes.description: Conversation-centric multi-stream processing that tracks changing positions of several speakers.

validation.summary: Commercial validation, with proprietary algorithms.

nodes.label: Oticon Intent DNN 2.0
nodes.description: Uses acoustic context plus motion and conversation sensors to drive an open-sound DNN processing strategy.

validation.summary: Strong audiology research framing; core model remains proprietary.

nodes.label: Widex Allure
nodes.description: Sound-quality-focused platform with speech enhancement marketed as Speech Enhancer Pro and AI-driven fitting assistance.

validation.summary: Commercial evidence; limited reproducible technical detail.

nodes.label: ReSound Vivia AI
nodes.description: Binaural commercial platform with a dedicated Deep Neural Network chip for speech in noise.

validation.summary: Deployed at scale; model details are proprietary.

nodes.label: Starkey Omega AI
nodes.description: On-device AI hearing platform combining speech processing, sensors and health-oriented features.

validation.summary: Commercial deployment; independent architectural evidence is limited.

nodes.label: AirPods Pro Hearing Aid Feature
nodes.description: Software-defined OTC hearing assistance integrated with a consumer earbud, hearing test and personalized profile.

validation.summary: Clinically evaluated and regulated; no access to the internal enhancement model.

nodes.label: sherpa-onnx
nodes.description: Cross-platform offline speech inference toolkit used by Melina to package and stream several denoising models.

validation.summary: Actively maintained cross-platform inference infrastructure.

nodes.label: ONNX Runtime
nodes.description: Execution layer behind Melina's portable model path on Android, Windows, macOS and Linux.

validation.summary: Mature cross-platform production runtime.

nodes.label: Tract · Sonos
nodes.description: Rust neural-network inference engine originated at Sonos. DeepFilterNet's libDF uses Tract; Melina carries a narrow tract-linalg Windows ARM64 compatibility patch.

validation.summary: Mature portable runtime used by libDF; Melina validates its Windows ARM64 assembler-selection patch in CI.

nodes.label: openMHA
nodes.description: Open modular hearing-aid platform with realtime audio graphs, fitting algorithms and binaural research configurations.

validation.summary: Purpose-built for hearing research and translational prototypes.

nodes.label: openMHA Example 34
nodes.description: Four-microphone binaural reference with three DNN enhancement approaches, including GCFnet and multichannel Wiener filtering.

validation.summary: Rare open binaural low-latency hearing configuration.

nodes.label: Clarity CEC3
nodes.description: Hearing-aid enhancement challenge with individualized listeners and a strict maximum 5 ms future-context rule.

validation.summary: The closest open benchmark to the target use case.

nodes.label: DNS Challenge
nodes.description: Microsoft-led datasets, evaluation tracks and DNSMOS tooling that shaped modern speech enhancement.

validation.summary: High coverage and adoption, but not hearing-loss-specific.

nodes.label: REAL-TSE 2026
nodes.description: Real-world target-speaker extraction challenge with enrollment, streaming baseline and domain-adaptation lessons.

validation.summary: Strong future benchmark for target-speaker systems; online track permits up to 100 ms.

nodes.label: WHAMR!
nodes.description: Noisy and reverberant multi-speaker benchmark used by Conv-TasNet and separation research.

validation.summary: Useful reproducible stress test; weaker match to live hearing devices.

nodes.label: Minimum-phase FIR
nodes.description: Directly predicts causal minimum-phase filters: a compelling route to sub-frame algorithmic delay.

nodes.label: Asymmetric STFT
nodes.description: Uses a short analysis window and longer synthesis context to reduce algorithmic delay while keeping frequency resolution.

nodes.label: ERB filterbank
nodes.description: Perceptually spaced auditory bands reduce compute and align controls with human frequency resolution.

nodes.label: Neural beamforming
nodes.description: A network predicts spatial filters or statistics while classical beamforming preserves controllability and cues.

nodes.label: SDW-MWF
nodes.description: Spatial distortion-weighted multichannel Wiener filtering balances noise reduction and target preservation.

nodes.label: CARFAC hearing model
nodes.description: Cascaded asymmetric resonators model cochlear processing and enable differentiable normal/impaired listeners.

nodes.label: Speaker embedding
nodes.description: Compact identity representation that conditions extraction on the listener's chosen voice.

nodes.label: Binaural cues · ITD/ILD
nodes.description: Interaural timing and level differences preserve localization and help separate competing sources.

nodes.label: WDRC & fitting
nodes.description: Wide dynamic range compression maps sound into an individual's residual audible range; enhancement must coexist with it.

nodes.label: Conv-TasNet
nodes.description: Learned time-domain analysis and temporal convolutional separation; causal details determine whether it can stream.

nodes.label: CRUSE
nodes.description: Convolutional recurrent U-Net family that trades feature-map width, recurrence and STFT delay for quality.
